meta.note: Starter content for a new install: the activity and lift catalogs, the rest card, and the non-climbing quota categories. Add achievements in the app, or import a plan from Settings. Generated by app/starter.build.mjs.

dailyMenu.name: Rest day
dailyMenu.dose: Nothing. Logged on purpose so it counts as a chosen day rather than a missed one — and so it is the one thing that does NOT mark the Move Every Day habit in Totem.
dailyMenu.whenInstead: Pick this deliberately when you're beat up, travelling, or sick. A rest day you chose is part of the plan; a rest day you fell into is not.

blocks.name: Nothing
steps: Log it and move on with your day.
If you want to do something: walk, stretch your hips, sleep an extra hour.
Do not 'just do a few easy hangs'. That is how a rest day becomes a light training day and stops being rest.

cues: Choosing this on purpose is a training decision. It keeps the streak and it keeps your fingers.

dailyMenu.name: Log a workout
dailyMenu.dose: Whatever you actually did. You picked the sport on the way in, so the form below is already the right shape — fill in as much or as little as you feel like. Log as many as you did; a ride and a swim is two of these, not one.
dailyMenu.whenInstead: This card replaced *Other training* on 2026-09-14, when the app stopped being a climbing log with a catch-all bolted on. The catch-all had nine activities and one form, so a lifting day was logged on a form asking its incline and a dance workout could not be logged at all — WHOOP had already recorded three sports (dance, mountain-biking, and its own generic "activity") that the card silently mapped to nothing. Now every sport has its own entry, its own icon, its own quota category and one of four form shapes. Pick the activity and the form follows it. Since 2026-09-17 you pick it BEFORE the card opens, off the + button: it is the same grouped, searchable screen as "pick a session", over the sports catalog instead of the plan’s own cards. If the workout is on WHOOP or Strava, attach it and the numbers fill themselves in. Two things it deliberately does NOT do: it never counts against your hard finger budget, because climbing is logged on the climbing cards where the budget can see it; and it is never recommended, because "do something" is not coaching. The one field worth being honest about is effort — a flat-out interval session and a coffee-shop spin are the same card and very different days.
dailyMenu.protocolNote: NO PROTOCOL, DELIBERATELY, since 2026-09-21. This card carried five steps of instructions about how to use the app, rendered as a tabbed reading view above the form on every single workout. A container card's content IS what the athlete logged into it, and the space the boilerplate occupied is now a free-text notes box in the log form (`out.notes`, the field retired in 2026-09-06 and brought back as a scratchpad rather than as "how did it feel"). The two cues that were worth keeping are in `dose` and `whenInstead` above, which is where a card explains itself.

outputs.label: What did you do?
outputs.hint: Search 91 activities — run, mountain bike, swim, dance, pickleball…

outputs.label: What did you lift?
outputs.hint: Search for the movement, say what you loaded it with, then log your sets.
outputs.musclesNote: Which muscles each movement works, for the body diagram — see app/src/lib/bodymap.jsx. Generated by app/muscles.build.mjs from free-exercise-db (public domain) and mapped onto react-body-highlighter's vocabulary; `from` records which dataset row each one came off, or `group:<name>` where nothing matched and the catalog group was used instead. Hand corrections are welcome and will survive nothing — re-running the script overwrites them, so correct the script if a mapping is wrong for everyone and the file if it is wrong for one movement you then stop regenerating.

dailyMenu.logFirstNote: The form leads this card and opens expanded, because the card has no protocol worth reading — its five steps are instructions for using the app, and the ride the athlete is logging is the point. Read by SessionSheet; see sessionlog.jsx on why the default is the other way round.

dailyMenu.name: Planned workout
dailyMenu.dose: A session somebody wrote down before you started it. The sets, the loads and the rests live on the entry itself — open it and the runner walks you through them one set at a time.
dailyMenu.whenInstead: Added 2026-09-17, when Today stopped recommending anything. So the app stopped guessing what the athlete should do and started helping them write down what the athlete decided to do. This card is the CONTAINER for that — it carries no protocol of its own, because the protocol is `data.plan` on the entry and is different every time. Everything else about it is the workout card: the activity decides the form, the quota category and the name, and WHOOP or Strava can still fill the numbers in. The difference is that it arrives with the work already written, and what it compares against is what it asked for rather than nothing.
dailyMenu.protocolNote: NO PROTOCOL, DELIBERATELY. A planned session IS its prescription — `data.plan` on the entry — and the sheet has always rendered that instead of this. What used to be here was five steps about how the runner works, never shown to anybody, kept in step with the app by nobody. Removed alongside the workout card's on 2026-09-21.

outputs.label: What kind of workout was this?
outputs.hint: Optional — it sets the form below and which quota this fills. A planned climbing session has no entry here; the plan already said what it was.

outputs.label: What did you lift?
outputs.hint: Search for the movement, say what you loaded it with, then log your sets.

dailyMenu.repeatViaNote: `sched.repeatVia` routes the day list’s "and another one" button to the screen that ASKS the question, instead of minting a blank entry of a card whose whole content comes from that question. `plan` opens the planner; `log` opens the activity chooser. A card without it gets the ordinary behaviour, which is right for anything that is a session in its own right.

recommender.stackRule: A day gets one main session plus up to two companions. A companion is never a hard finger session, never finger work on a day that already has finger work unless the plan declares the pairing (sched.stacksWith), never at a venue you aren't at, and never something mutex with what's already on the day. It also has to be genuinely owed rather than merely legal, inside 45 spare minutes.
recommender.stackWhy: The week owes more work than it has days — core, hips, eccentrics, antagonists, sub-threshold hangs and the lead laps all want a slot. Recommending one session a day meant the short non-finger blocks were quietly dropped, or found by hand in the swap list. Stacking them is safe in a way that adding training days is not: the hard-finger budget is counted per DAY, so a 13-minute hip block on an existing training day costs nothing against it. Under quotas this matters more, not less — a quota is a count of WORKOUTS, and a day that holds a ride and a lift fills two of them.
recommender.rule: Three hard finger days per week maximum, never on consecutive days. Two is still what a normal week plans for; the third exists so a week that moved around — a gym night with friends, a missed Monday — does not have to be paid for by skipping the work.
recommender.why: The old rule was two per week, 72 hours apart. That is inside what the literature actually tested (every hangboard RCT used 2-3 sessions per week), so the change costs nothing in evidence terms. The spacing is the part that genuinely changed: three exposures cannot sit 72 hours apart inside seven days, so the gap rule drops to 48 hours. That is defensible rather than arbitrary — tendon collagen data suggest net matrix degradation for roughly 36 hours after a loading bout, and 48 hours clears it — but it is a weaker guarantee than 72, and back-to-back is now the hard block because it is the one that stacks loading inside the degradation window.
recommender.coachRule: The coach may add or subtract at most `coachCap` points from any session, and must say why. It cannot lift a hard block — the spacing rule and the weekly cap are enforced before any weight is read, so no coach note can put two hard finger days back to back.
recommender.workoutModeRule: Workout mode is offered only where a session DECLARES something for a clock to run: a `protocol.blocks[].timer`/`timers`, or a rest the session logs for itself (`setRest`, which is what gives the 4×4s their countdown). With no interval every phase counts up, nothing advances itself, and the mode is a full-screen wrapper around a set log. Doubled lead laps are the case that settled it — the five minutes between doubles is real programming, but nobody stands at a wall driving a timer through it, and on-the-wall work gets logged afterwards. Adding a timer to a session turns the mode on with no rebuild; `logSpec.workout: true|false` overrides the guess where the interval is a bad proxy for whether it would actually help. Losing the mode never costs a session its set log.
recommender.whoopSportRule: A session declares `sched.whoopSport` when it is the kind of thing WHOOP gives a name to — "climbing" on the nine sessions that put them on a wall. It is how the app suggests which of the evening's WHOOP workouts WAS this session: a workout titled rock-climbing or bouldering on a climbing night agrees with the session about what happened, and one titled Weightlifting contradicts it and is never suggested however well the clock lines up. Declared rather than inferred from `venue`, because the grip economy drill is on a wall at the gym and crimp crawls are on a stair at home and the venue cannot tell them apart. A session that declares nothing gets no opinion, which is the same ranking the app did before this existed. Attaching is still always a tap — see `whoopRule`.
recommender.whoopRule: WHOOP describes last night, so it is the weakest term in the engine and is capped BELOW the coach at `whoop.cap` points against score gaps of forty. `lowRecovery` and `highRecovery` are WHOOP's own red and green bands; `hrvDrop` is the percentage under THE ATHLETE'S OWN fortnight median that counts as suppressed, never a population figure. Two independent signals agreeing — a red recovery AND a suppressed HRV — count for full weight, either alone for 60% of it. Like the coach's nudges these are read after the hard blocks have already returned, so no reading can put two hard finger days back to back, breach the weekly cap, or offer a gym session on a night the athlete is at home. A red morning also cannot decide the day is a rest day: it makes rest score better, and pressing the button stays their. No reading at all — no band worn, WHOOP still calibrating, nothing pulled — computes exactly what the app computed before WHOOP existed, which is pinned in recommend.test.js.
recommender.whoopEvidence: Read the deviation, not the number. WHOOP's recovery score is a proprietary composite with no published validation against training readiness, and the HRV underneath it (rmssd, measured during slow-wave sleep) has genuine day-to-day meaning against a personal baseline and almost none as an absolute. Nothing here is evidence that training against a recovery score improves an outcome — no trial has shown that in climbers or anyone else. It is in the engine because it is a cheap daily reading of something the plan already cares about, and it is capped low because that is exactly how much confidence it deserves.
recommender.venueRule: Venue is no longer a branch. Where the athlete is comes off the check-in and acts as a FILTER on the quota board — a gym session is hidden, not penalised, on an evening the athlete has said the athlete is home. A penalty every survivor pays decides no ranking, and "Tuesday isn't a gym day" was never a fact about Tuesday.
recommender.quotaRule: A quota is a count of workouts in a category for the current Monday-to-Sunday week. Misses expire on Sunday rather than carrying as debt — a week that went badly should not make the next one look worse than it is. Quotas replaced the per-weekday template on 2026-09-14: the template named one session per weekday per branch, which meant a Thursday the athlete could not make cost the board session rather than moving it.

checkin.title: Check in with your coach
checkin.intro: Tell it how you are and what the day looks like. It reads your log and your profile, answers you, and can put sessions in front of you with a button to swap one in as your main or add it as an extra. It never changes your day on its own — nothing moves until you press something, and anything you press can be undone.
checkin.placeholder: can't get to the gym tonight — going Sunday instead. Fingers feel fine.
starters: Can't train today — what should I move?
Feeling wrecked. Is today worth doing?
What's this week actually owe me?

fields.label: Where you are
fields.note: Two gyms, since 2026-09-14. The CLIMBING gym is where the board, the wall and the laps are; the plain gym is the weights room, where the only thing the menu offers is a lift and the support blocks. Saying the wrong one costs you nothing permanent — every lane stays tappable with its reason on it.

checkin.note: The fields are the things a coach would ask before saying anything, and they are hard fields rather than prose because bodyweight is a series, and 'feeling' is only useful if it is comparable across days. Three of them are read by the recommendation engine itself (`informs`): where you are replaces the calendar's guess about the day, the time you have rules out anything longer, and your fingers right now override what your last session logged. Everything else goes in the message. What you say here is kept — every check-in is read by the next one, so telling the coach on Thursday that the gym has moved to Sunday is what makes Sunday's plan right.

outputsNote: Two of these appear on every session — how hard it felt, and how your fingers felt after. They are what make the trend charts work: RPE times duration gives session training load, and the finger score is your earliest warning that the two-hard-days budget is being broken. Fill them in the moment you finish; recalled RPE from the next morning is worth much less. Every session also ends with two free-text notes — how it felt, and what to change next time. Those are the ones worth writing properly: when you repeat a session the app shows you the last one before you start, which is the only moment 'what to improve' can actually change anything.
menuNote: Thirty sessions, each tagged with the quota category it fills. The climbing ones carry protocols because a repeater set is meaningless without its numbers; *Log a workout* carries none, because a ride is a ride. Nothing here is scheduled to a weekday any more — the week asks for counts per category and you decide which day each lands on.

quotaCategories.name: Swim
quotaCategories.blurb: Pool and open water. The discipline with the most technique per hour and the least transfer from everything else you do.
quotaCategories.logNote: No protocol, because a swim is a swim. This lane opens the workout card with the activity already picked.

quotaCategories.name: Bike
quotaCategories.blurb: Road, gravel, mountain, trainer. The biggest block of a half iron by time, and currently the one you actually enjoy — most of these can be rides for fun and still count.
quotaCategories.logNote: No protocol, because a bike is a bike. This lane opens the workout card with the activity already picked.

quotaCategories.name: Run
quotaCategories.blurb: Road, trail, treadmill, track. The discipline that punishes a jump in volume hardest, so raise this quota slower than it feels like you could.
quotaCategories.logNote: No protocol, because a run is a run. This lane opens the workout card with the activity already picked.

quotaCategories.name: Lift
quotaCategories.blurb: Resistance work of any kind. Serves both goals and belongs to neither.
quotaCategories.logNote: No protocol, because a lift is a lift. This lane opens the workout card with the activity already picked.

quotaCategories.name: Support
quotaCategories.blurb: Core, hips, antagonists, eccentrics, mobility, the warm-up. Small, unglamorous, and the first thing to disappear from a busy week.

quotaCategories.name: Anything else
quotaCategories.blurb: Dance, pickleball, a hike, manual labour. Here so a day you moved is a day that counts, and so you can set a quota for it if you want one.
quotaCategories.logNote: Nothing in the menu is a "misc" session — this lane opens the workout card and lets you search.

formShapes.name: Distance cardio
formShapes.blurb: Miles, time, and the pace that falls out of them. Elevation and incline appear only for the activities that have them.

formShapes.name: Pool
formShapes.blurb: Yards and laps rather than miles, because that is how a pool is actually counted, with a per-100 pace derived from the time.

formShapes.name: Lift
formShapes.blurb: The exercise chooser — search the movement, say what you loaded it with, log the sets.

formShapes.name: Time only
formShapes.blurb: How long, how hard. For everything whose distance is meaningless: dance, yoga, pickleball, an hour of manual labour.

quickNames.note: Names for ONE logged workout, offered as taps so a rename costs no typing. Content, so the vocabulary grows with no rebuild. The labels deliberately echo plannerKinds: a ride the athlete PLANNED as 'Zone 2 ride' and one the athlete renames afterwards should read the same in the log. `casual` is the name a 'just miles' entry gives itself (a commute, for example), keyed by discipline so a walk marked just miles is not called a commute; it is recorded as `out.titleFrom: 'casual'` and taken back if the athlete unticks the box, and it never touches a name the athlete typed. `warmup` is the name the third button on the unlogged-workout card gives itself — — recorded the same way (`out.titleFrom: 'warmup'`) and, like a commute, kept out of the quotas and out of the training load, because ten minutes on the rower before a lift is not a rowing workout.

gearKinds.name: Bike
gearKinds.blurb: Road, gravel, mountain, trainer. Strava keeps the odometer.

gearKinds.name: Running shoes
gearKinds.blurb: Miles are the whole point — this is the number that says when to replace them.

gearKinds.name: Climbing shoes
gearKinds.blurb: Time on the wall. Resoles are a function of hours, not of dates.

gearKinds.name: Rope
gearKinds.blurb: Hours under load, plus the date it came out of the bag — a rope ages whether you climb on it or not.

gearKinds.name: Board & hangboard
gearKinds.blurb: The Port-A-Board, a hangboard, a portable edge.

gearKinds.name: Measurement
gearKinds.blurb: The Tindeq and anything else that produces a number rather than a session.

gearKinds.name: Weights
gearKinds.blurb: Plates, bars, dumbbells, a dip belt. Counted in time AND in reps, because a 40-minute session and 300 reps are different kinds of wear.

gearNote: Bikes and shoes come from Strava, odometers and all, and stay read-only here — Strava keeps counting them and two sources of truth for one number is one too many. Everything else you add yourself, and the app counts its use out of what you log. A piece of gear can be the DEFAULT for its kind, which is how a logged ride picks up your primary bike with no taps; anything you actually rode instead, you change on the workout.

journal.note: Nothing here is on until you turn it on. Pick the handful you are actually curious about — a journal with forty questions is a journal you answer once. Anything you track gets compared against the next morning’s recovery once there are enough days to say something.

behaviours.label: Went to bed later than usual

plannerKinds.note: What the + button offers when the athlete asks for a workout to be planned. CONTENT, like everything else here — the list of things the athlete plans is a list that will be wrong the day it ships, and adding "Shoulders" should be an edit to this file rather than a rebuild. `prompt` is the phrase handed to the planner as the session kind; `category` and `activity` are what the entry fills if the planner does not name its own — and a kind that leaves BOTH null (the sport-agnostic endurance kinds, the climbing kinds) is telling the planner to decide, which for endurance means picking swim, bike or run from what the week still owes. — so the Endurance group leads with those and the hard kinds say how rarely they belong.

kinds.label: Legs
kinds.prompt: a lower-body lifting session
kinds.hint: squat, hinge, single-leg, calves

kinds.label: Push
kinds.prompt: an upper-body push lifting session
kinds.hint: chest, shoulders, triceps

kinds.label: Pull
kinds.prompt: an upper-body pull lifting session
kinds.hint: back, biceps, rear delts

kinds.label: Full body
kinds.prompt: a full-body lifting session
kinds.hint: one big push, one big pull, one hinge

kinds.label: Core & hips
kinds.prompt: a core, hip and antagonist session
kinds.hint: the unglamorous stuff that disappears from a busy week

kinds.label: Zone 2
kinds.prompt: a zone 2 aerobic session — easy, steady, conversational — in whichever of swim, bike or run the week still owes most (say which you picked and why in `why`, and do not repeat yesterday's sport unless the week asks for it)
kinds.hint: easy, steady, conversational — most of your week should be this

kinds.label: Long & easy
kinds.prompt: the week's longest aerobic session, still zone 2 throughout, in whichever of bike or run the week most needs — with fuelling and a pacing cue
kinds.hint: the week's longest, still easy — it picks the sport that needs it

kinds.label: Recovery
kinds.prompt: a genuinely easy recovery session, 20–40 minutes, zone 1 to low zone 2, in whichever of swim, bike or run costs the legs least today
kinds.hint: very easy spin, jog or swim — shake the legs out

kinds.label: Tempo / sweet spot
kinds.prompt: a tempo or sweet-spot aerobic session — 20–40 minutes of sustained work just below threshold — in the sport the week most needs it; this is one of at most one or two hard endurance sessions a week
kinds.hint: steady-hard, 20–40 min of work — once a week at most

kinds.label: Threshold
kinds.prompt: a threshold session — cruise intervals at about an hour's best effort with short rests — in the sport the week most needs it
kinds.hint: cruise intervals at about an hour's best effort, short rests

kinds.label: VO2 intervals
kinds.prompt: a VO2max interval session — 3 to 5 minute hard efforts with roughly equal rest — in the sport the week most needs it; rare, and only if the week has had its easy volume
kinds.hint: 3–5 min hard, equal rest — rare, and only after the easy volume is in

kinds.label: Hills
kinds.prompt: a hill session — repeats on a real climb, or a low-cadence climbing block on the trainer — ride or run, whichever the week needs
kinds.hint: hill repeats, ride or run — strength you can breathe through

kinds.label: Brick
kinds.prompt: a brick: a bike block straight into a run block, written as TWO blocks with category bike and category run respectively, mostly easy with the transition rehearsed
kinds.hint: bike, then straight onto a run — how the race actually goes

kinds.label: Race rehearsal
kinds.prompt: a half-iron race rehearsal piece — a portion of the swim, bike or run (whichever the week most needs) at the pace the athlete could hold for that leg's race distance, bracketed by easy work
kinds.hint: a piece of one leg at the pace you could hold for the whole thing

kinds.label: Swim
kinds.prompt: a pool swim session written as a set list
kinds.hint: whatever the pool needs today — warm-up, main set, cool-down, in yards

kinds.label: Easy swim
kinds.prompt: an easy continuous swim — zone 2 in the water, long relaxed strokes, in yards
kinds.hint: continuous easy laps — zone 2 in the water

kinds.label: Technique
kinds.prompt: a swim technique session — drills for catch, breathing and body position, short pieces with full rest; distance is not the point
kinds.hint: drills — catch, breathing, body position; distance is not the point

kinds.label: Endurance swim
kinds.prompt: an endurance swim — long steady sets building toward 1.2 miles continuous, in yards
kinds.hint: long steady sets, building toward 1.2 miles without stopping

kinds.label: CSS / threshold
kinds.prompt: a critical-swim-speed set — 100s and 200s at CSS pace with short rest, in yards
kinds.hint: 100s and 200s at critical swim speed, short rest

kinds.label: Open-water skills
kinds.prompt: an open-water skills swim — sighting every few strokes, drafting, swimming straight without a lane line, with an easy aerobic base
kinds.hint: sighting, drafting, swimming straight — outside if you can

kinds.label: Ride
kinds.prompt: a bike session written as intervals
kinds.hint: indoor or road, by time and effort

kinds.label: Zone 2 ride
kinds.prompt: a zone 2 ride — steady, conversational, by time and heart rate or power
kinds.hint: the half iron's biggest block — an easy hour or three

kinds.label: Long ride
kinds.prompt: the week's long ride — zone 2 throughout, fuelling every 30 minutes, with the last stretch at race-day effort only if the athlete is fresh
kinds.hint: the week's longest — eat every 30 minutes

kinds.label: Sweet spot
kinds.prompt: a sweet-spot ride — 2 to 3 blocks of 10 to 20 minutes just under threshold with easy spinning between
kinds.hint: 2–3 × 10–20 min just under threshold

kinds.label: VO2 intervals
kinds.prompt: a VO2max bike session — 4 to 6 × 3 to 5 minutes hard with equal easy spinning between
kinds.hint: 4–6 × 3–5 min hard, equal rest

kinds.label: Hill repeats
kinds.prompt: a bike hill session — seated and standing climbing repeats, or a low-cadence climbing block on the trainer
kinds.hint: seated and standing climbs, or low cadence on the trainer

kinds.label: Recovery spin
kinds.prompt: a recovery spin — 30 to 45 minutes, legs turning, high cadence, nothing else
kinds.hint: 30–45 min, legs turning, nothing else

kinds.label: Trainer session
kinds.prompt: a structured indoor trainer session by time and effort, with a proper warm-up and a cadence cue on every piece
kinds.hint: structured indoor, by time and effort

kinds.label: Cadence & skills
kinds.prompt: a bike skills session — high-cadence spin-ups, single-leg drills and aero holds inside an easy ride
kinds.hint: spin-ups, single-leg drills, aero holds, inside an easy ride

kinds.label: Run
kinds.prompt: a run session written as intervals
kinds.hint: easy, tempo, intervals or long

kinds.label: Easy run
kinds.prompt: an easy zone 2 run — conversational the whole way, by time rather than pace
kinds.hint: conversational, zone 2 — the run that builds the rest

kinds.label: Long run
kinds.prompt: the week's long run — easy throughout, no more than a quarter longer than their longest run of the last three weeks
kinds.hint: the week's longest, easy — raise it slower than it feels like you could

kinds.label: Tempo run
kinds.prompt: a tempo run — 20 to 30 minutes comfortably hard between an easy warm-up and cool-down
kinds.hint: 20–30 min comfortably hard

kinds.label: Intervals
kinds.prompt: a run interval session — 400s to 1000s, or 3 to 5 minute pieces, with real recovery between
kinds.hint: 400s to 1000s, or 3–5 min pieces, with real rest

kinds.label: Hill repeats
kinds.prompt: a run hill session — short steep repeats, walk or jog down, inside an easy run
kinds.hint: short steep repeats, walk down

kinds.label: Strides
kinds.prompt: an easy run finished with 6 to 8 × 20 second fast, relaxed strides with full recovery
kinds.hint: an easy run finished with 6–8 × 20 s fast and relaxed

kinds.label: Trail run
kinds.prompt: an easy trail run by time, walking the steep parts, effort not pace
kinds.hint: by time, not pace — walk the steep bits

kinds.label: Run-walk
kinds.prompt: a run-walk base session — for example run 4 minutes, walk 1, repeated — to build running volume without the injury
kinds.hint: run 4, walk 1 — volume without the injury

kinds.label: Treadmill
kinds.prompt: a treadmill run — incline walking, easy running or intervals by time and grade
kinds.hint: incline or intervals, when weather or daylight say so

plannerKinds.goalPlaceholder: "squat has stalled", "legs are wrecked, keep it light", "two hours free, want it all easy", "build to race pace"…
plannerKinds.groupNote: The dividers on the plan-a-workout picker. Ordered as written; a kind whose `group` names nothing here falls into a trailing "Anything else" section rather than disappearing, which is what the reachability test in smoke.jsx pins. `collapsed: true` folds a group behind its header with a count — every kind is still in the page and still reachable, it is one tap further. The sport catalogs are folded because the sport-agnostic kinds above them are the bread and butter and thirty cards of ride variants above the climbing section would bury it.

groups.name: Endurance
groups.blurb: These let the model pick swim, bike or run for you, from what the week still owes — build it yourself and you say which. Zone 2 and easy volume are the bread and butter; the hard ones say how rarely they belong.
